_comment: One publish on the wire, exactly as the client posts it to POST /v1/sessions/publish (ST-093, ST-094).
Read by both ends and by neither's production code, like summarize-request.v1.json: the client's
sender writes this shape, the backend's PublishBundle reads it, and the field names ARE the contract.
TheContractIsWhatPublishAccepts (backend) and ClientWritesThePublishContract (client) notice drift.
`company` is the PSA's name for the ticket's company, as the search returned it; the backend maps it to
the documentation platform's company for a knowledge-base article (ST-097) and never stores the ticket.
The note is the session.v1 draft as edited in Review: a step carries `confirmed` when the technician
checked it and `transcript_refs` when it quotes the transcript, and omits both otherwise. The frames are the included ones only, in strip
order, each as base64 bytes -- already redacted on the device (INV-1) and held by the backend for this
request only (INV-7). The image here is eight bytes of JPEG header: the shape is under test, not a
picture. Destinations name what to publish; the response answers each one separately so a retry
can send only what failed.
A destination whose note or article landed but whose screenshots did not all attach is `ok: true` with
its id and `kind: partial`, and `error` says which screenshots are missing: it is on the ticket, so a
retry must not send it again. One that had not answered by the publish deadline is `ok: false` with
`kind: timed_out`, and may have landed, so `retryable` is false and `error` says to check first.
One that was sent and answered with something that could not be read is `kind: unknown`, the same
way and for the same reason: it is the kind a provider gives any write that may have been saved.
`response_uncertain` shows both. The deadline counts from when the request
arrived, so a body that took all of it to upload sends nothing: each destination is then `ok: false`
with `kind: unavailable` and `retryable: true`, and `error` says nothing was sent.
